title: SAML & SCIM Configuration Guide for Google Workspace

blocks.text: This guide illustrates how to configure Google Workspace as the identity provider (IdP) for the Zscaler service.
The SAML features supported by the Zscaler and Google Workspace integration are:

blocks.item: SP-initiated SSO
To perform SP-initiated SSO:
Open your site.
You are redirected to https://gateway.<Zscaler Cloud Name>.net and prompted for a username.
Enter your User Name and click Sign in.
Just-in-Time (JIT) Provisioning (SAML auto-provisioning)

blocks.text: The SCIM features supported by the Zscaler and Google Workspace integration are:

blocks.item: Create Users
Update User Attributes
Deactivate Users

blocks.text: Google Workspace does not support the following features:

blocks.item: Sign SAML Request
On-Demand Provisioning for Users
Group Push

blocks.text: Ensure that you have the following to configure Google Workspace as the IdP:

blocks.item: Google Workspace account with admin privileges
The Zscaler SAML certificate (See Adding Identity Providers.)

blocks.heading: Configuring Google Workspace as the IdP for the Zscaler Service

blocks.text: To configure Google Workspace as the IdP for the Zscaler service:

blocks.item: 1. Configure the Zscaler app in the Google Admin console.
Sign in to the Google Admin console.
In the Google Admin console, go to Apps > Web and mobile apps.
See image.
In the Add app drop-down, select Search for apps.
See image.
Enter Zscaler in the search bar and click Select for the Zscaler web app.
See image.
On the Google Identity Provider details page, do the following, then click CONTINUE:
Copy the SSO URL. You need it when configuring Google Workspace as the IdP for the Zscaler service.
Download or copy the Certificate. You need it when configuring Google Workspace as the IdP for the Zscaler service.
Ensure the certificate file name:
Has a .pem extension (e.g., rename it to google.pem). The Zscaler service only accepts certificates with the .pem extension.
By default, Windows hides extensions for known file types.
Change the Windows Folder Properties to View and Edit Extensions
Start the Windows Control Panel.
Go to Appearance & Personalization > File Explorer Options.
When the File Explorer Options window appears, click the View tab.
In Advanced settings, deselect Hide extensions for known file types to view extensions.
See image.
Rename the certificate to change the extension.
Contains only one dot (".").
See image.
See image.
On the Service provider details page, enter the following, then click CONTINUE:
ACS URL: Enter https://login.<Zscaler cloud name>.net:443/sfc_sso.

Entity ID: Enter your <Zscaler cloud name>. To learn how you can find your cloud name, see Understanding Zscaler Cloud Names. In this example, the cloud is Zscaler Two, so the Entity ID is zscalertwo.net.

If you have more than one organization instance on the same Zscaler cloud, you must use an org-specific entity ID. You can see the org-specific entity ID for your instance in the Zscaler Admin Console while adding or editing an identity provider.
The org-specific entity ID is formatted like the following example:
https://login.zscalertwo.net/sfc_sso/3829920
Name ID format: In the drop-down menu, select EMAIL.
Name ID: In the drop-down menu, select Basic Information > Primary email.
See image.
On the Attribute mapping page, in the Attributes section:
Select Department in the Google directory attributes drop-down menu and enter Department in App attributes.
Select First name in the Google directory attributes drop-down menu and enter DisplayName in App attributes.
See image.
Click FINISH.
2. Add Google Workspace as the IdP in the Zscaler Admin Console.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Internet & SaaS Authentication > Internet Authentication Settings > Identity Providers.
Click Add IdP.
If you have an existing IdP configuration, the What do you want to do? window appears. Click Add another SAML IdP for a subset of users or locations and then Next.
See image.
In the Add IdP window:
SAML Portal URL: Enter the SSO URL that you copied from the Google Admin console.
Login Name Attribute: Enter NameID (case-sensitive).
IdP SAML Certificate: Upload the .pem certificate that you downloaded from the Google Admin console.

Org-Specific Entity ID: Enable if you have more than one organization instance on the same Zscaler cloud. For example, if you have two organization instances on the same Zscaler cloud and must authenticate both instances against the same Google account, you can't use the same entity ID for multiple apps in the Google Admin console. For this situation, you must enable this setting for both instances to generate a unique org-specific entity ID.

Locations: Select the locations to map to this IdP. You can also search for a location. Any unselected locations are mapped to the default IdP. This field is set to Any for the default IdP, and you can't modify it.

Authentication Domains: Select the domains to map to this IdP. This allows the Zscaler service to display the correct IdP to authenticate an incoming user. Any unselected domains are mapped to the default IdP. This field is set to Any for the default IdP, and you can't modify it. Apart from the default IdP, any additional IdPs must be mapped to at least one domain.
Vendor: Select Google Apps.
See image.
(Optional) If you want to configure SAML Auto-Provisioning, in the Provisioning Options section:
Enable SAML Auto-Provisioning: Enable this option.
User Display Name Attribute: Enter DisplayName (case-sensitive).
Group Name Attribute: (Optional) Specify a group name attribute or leave this field blank.
Department Name Attribute: Enter Department (case-sensitive).
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
To learn more about configuring an IdP in the Zscaler Admin Console, see Adding Identity Providers.
3. Enable SAML in the Zscaler Admin Console.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Internet & SaaS Authentication > Internet Authentication Settings > Default Settings.

For Authentication Frequency, select how often users are required to authenticate to the Zscaler service. If you select Custom, the Custom Authentication Frequency (days) field appears. Specify 1 to 180 days. To learn more, see About Authentication Default Settings.
For Authentication Type, choose SAML.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
4. Enable SCIM in the Zscaler Admin Console.
From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Internet & SaaS Authentication > Internet Authentication Settings > Identity Providers.
Click the Edit icon for your previously configured Google IdP.
In the Edit IdP window, select Enable SCIM Provisioning.
Copy the Base URL and Bearer Token. You need them to configure SCIM in the Google Admin console.
See image.
Click Save and activate the change.
5. Configure SCIM in the Google Admin console.
In the Google Admin console, go to Apps > Web and mobile apps and select the previously configured Zscaler app.
On the home page for the Zscaler app, click Configure auto-provisioning.
See image.
On the App authorization page, enter the Bearer Token you copied from the Zscaler Admin Console, then click CONTINUE.
See image.
On the Endpoint URL page, enter the Base URL you copied from the Zscaler Admin Console, then click CONTINUE.
See image.
On the Attribute mapping page, configure the attributes so they match the following table, then click CONTINUE:
See image.
(Optional) On the Provisioning scope (optional) page, search for and select a group if you want to limit provisioning to a specific group instead of all users, then click CONTINUE.
On the Deprovisioning page, specify an action and time for:
When an app is turned off for a user
When a user is suspended from Google
When a user is deleted from Google
See image.
Click FINISH.
On the home page for the Zscaler app, click TEST SAML LOGIN.
See image.
In the Can't test SAML login window, click ALLOW ACCESS.
See image.
In the Service status option, select ON for everyone.
See image.
Click SAVE.
On the home page for the Zscaler app, enable Auto-provisioning.
See image.
The Turn on window appears.
Click TURN ON.
See image.
6. Configure the Zscaler Authentication Exemptions List.
To configure the list and enable users access to Google Workspace:
From the navigation menu, go to Internet Access > Setting > Advanced Settings.
In the Authentication Exemptions section, enter accounts.google.com in Exempted URLs.
Click Save and activate the change.
If you are using PAC files, enter the following exception to the PAC file exemption list. Otherwise, the authentication fails.
If (shExpMatch(host, "accounts.google.com")) return "DIRECT";
This option only applies to user traffic from known locations. To learn more, see Exempting URLs and Cloud Apps from Authentication.

blocks.heading: Testing the SAML and SCIM Configuration

blocks.text: When your configuration is complete, you can test your work on another device.
Test the SAML configuration with one or both of the following methods:

blocks.item: Test the SAML Configuration by Logging Out of the Zscaler Service

This testing method only applies if you're forwarding traffic using PAC files, Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) tunnels, or IPSec tunnels, and you've enabled Enforce Authentication for the location or sublocation.
On the device, browse to ip.zscaler.com.
If you are already logged in to the Zscaler service, click Logout. Otherwise, ensure that your traffic is being forwarded to the Zscaler service.
Browse to a website. You are redirected to Google and prompted to log in.
Log in using your Google credentials, and you are automatically redirected to the original URL request.
Go to ip.zscaler.com. The status window shows the username indicating that authentication was successful.
Test the SAML Configuration with the Test URL

On the device, enter https://login.<Zscaler cloud Name>/clstart?version=1&_domain=<Tenant Domain>&redrurl=https://mobile.<Zscaler cloud Name>. To learn how you can find your cloud name, see Understanding Zscaler Cloud Names. The <Tenant Domain> is your organization's domain that is used to log in to the Zscaler service. For example, if you logged in to the Zscaler service with the username admin@zscaler.com, then zscaler.com is your <Tenant Domain>.
Given an organization on the zscalerbeta.net cloud with zscaler.com as the <Tenant Domain>, the completed URL would be:
https://login.zscalerbeta.net/clstart?version=1&_domain=zscaler.com&redrurl=https://mobile.zscalerbeta.net
If you are redirected to the Zscaler Admin Console, the SAML configuration is successful. You might be prompted to authenticate with your IdP.

blocks.text: To test the SCIM configuration, in the Zscaler Admin Console, go to Administration > Internet & SaaS Authentication > Internet & SaaS Users. You should see a complete list of the users and groups added to your user database.
If any errors occur, see Troubleshooting SAML to troubleshoot browser settings and SAML error codes.
